hosting.//site: Two hosting sites live in this project. Without this key `firebase deploy` picks the one matching the project id (theprime-construction), which is not the canonical site — naming it here is what makes `pnpm run deploy:web` land in the right place.

headers.//: Firebase defaults every file to max-age=3600, which is exactly wrong for the two kinds of file here. The catch-all governs the HTML; the rules after it override it for anything content-addressed. Order matters — later matches win.
headers.//max-age: 0 — the browser revalidates on every navigation, so a deploy is visible immediately rather than up to an hour later. That was the original bug: a fresh tab loaded the previous build straight after a release.
headers.//s-maxage: 600 — but the edge still serves it. Plain `no-cache` here was a mistake: it stopped Fastly caching the HTML at all, so every visitor paid a trip to origin and TTFB went from ~40ms to ~250ms. Firebase purges its CDN on deploy, so the ten minutes is a backstop for a failed purge, not the release delay.

headers.//: Filenames carry a content hash, so a changed file is a different URL and this can never serve something stale. Without it a returning visitor kept the previous deploy's bundle for up to an hour — which is how the old build survived a deploy and loaded from cache in testing.
The Draco decoder is pinned to the three version in package.json and only changes when that does.

Font filenames encode family, subset, weight range and style, so a different font is a different file. These are the one asset a returning visitor should never re-fetch. Swapping a font means changing the filename, not just the bytes.
